hypothesis: Deep-subagent navigation (subagents view, open child chat, go to parent) in deep trees: the passive roster walk's legacy registry probe (legacy_registry_path) read each live child's parent transcript WHOLE to extract the header id parsed off the first line, once per parent per walk => every saved-catalog fetch (list_saved_sessions, list --all) scanned linear in the family's total transcript bytes; deep families of large parents paid pathological catalog latency.
approach: Bound the probe to the file's first line (read_first_line_bounded, 64KiB cap - the same helper/precedent the bounded session-list header read uses): same header id, one line of IO. crates/pa-daemon/src/rlm_ledger.rs fn legacy_registry_path + unit test (over-long first line reads as absent; a parent far past the cap still resolves). Diff vs d5cd4b132 (rust tip at fold time): +51/-3, one file; identical diff vs bbb886dd8 on the 22f2a434c fold.
parity_notes: No wire, prompt, schema, or user-visible change on any path that does not hit the legacy registry probe. Judgment change is disclosed and tested: (1) a first line longer than 64KiB now reads as absent (base parsed it after reading the whole file - far past any real session header, same class as the 512-byte list gate); (2) a corrupt tail no longer masks a readable header (display-grade metadata either way). read_first_line_bounded is pre-existing upstream code with its own test coverage (bounded matches, unterminated, CRLF, empty, over-long).
